entities.title: CivilDate examples
entities.summary: Making dates, refusing ones that can't exist, weekday and ISO week, adding days and months, counting days and ordering, compared with datetime.date and calendar.
criteria: CivilDate.of creates the date when the fields name a real day.
CivilDate.of accepts 29 February when the year is a leap year.
CivilDate.of accepts 29 February when the year is a century divisible by 400.
CivilDate.of raises a ValueError, with the reason, when the day does not exist in the month.
CivilDate.of creates the date when the year is beyond 9999.
CivilDate.of creates the date when the year is before year 1.
CivilDate.try_of returns invalid when the day is 30 February.
CivilDate.try_of returns invalid when 29 February falls in a common year.
CivilDate.try_of returns invalid when 29 February falls in a century not divisible by 400.
CivilDate.try_of returns invalid when the month is 13.
CivilDate.parse returns the date when the text is an ISO 8601 calendar date.
CivilDate.parse returns invalid, with the reason, when the text names a day that does not exist.
CivilDate.day_of_week returns the weekday of the date, numbered as in ISO 8601.
CivilDate.iso_week returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date.
CivilDate.is_leap_year follows the Gregorian leap-year rules for every kind of year.
CivilDate.add_days returns the date that many days later, carrying into the next month.
CivilDate.add_months returns none when the day is missing from the target month.
CivilDate.add_months with MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN returns the last day of the target month when the day is missing from it.
CivilDate.add returns none when a one-month period lands on a missing day.
CivilDate.days_until returns the number of days to a later date.
CivilDate's less-than operator is true when the left date comes first.

CivilDateTime.in_zone keeps the wall time and the zone name as an intention.
CivilDateTime.at_offset pins the wall time to a fixed UTC offset.

entities.title: ZonedIntent examples
entities.summary: Resolving a wall time in a zone, in a gap and in an overlap, with and without policies, and adding a day across a DST change.
criteria: ZonedIntent.resolve returns the one instant when the wall time happens exactly once.
ZonedIntent.resolve returns none when the wall time falls in a daylight-saving gap.
ZonedIntent.resolve with Gap.SHIFT_FORWARD moves the wall time forward by the length of the gap.
ZonedIntent.resolve returns both instants when the wall time happens twice.
ZonedIntent.resolve with Overlap.EARLIEST returns the first of the two instants.
ZonedIntent.add_days keeps the wall time when the day crosses a daylight-saving change.

entities.title: Instant examples
entities.summary: Instants from clock readings, exact fractions and differences, POSIX versus SI seconds, and an instant seen in a zone.
criteria: Instant.from_unix_nanoseconds takes a clock reading as an input when the program reads the clock.
Instant.from_unix_seconds returns the Unix epoch when given zero seconds.
Instant.from_unix_seconds keeps all nine fractional digits when given nanoseconds.
Instant.from_unix_seconds keeps a fraction of a second when given one.
Instant.until returns the exact number of seconds, as a fraction, between two instants.
Instant.until returns 23 hours when the instants are noon on both sides of a spring-forward night.
Instant.add with POSIX seconds moves the instant by exactly that many seconds.
Instant.add with SI seconds returns unsupported when no leap-second table is available.
Instant.in_zone returns the wall time and offset in the zone when the zone has rules for it.
